guideTitle: 6 Best Portable Chargers With Built-In Cables (2026)
metaTitle: Best Portable Chargers With Built-In Cables
metaDescription: Six portable chargers with built-in cables compared on cable types, fast charging, capacity, and extras like AC wall plugs, to help you pick well.
mainKeyword: best portable chargers with built in cables
introParagraphs: A portable charger with built-in cables solves the most common failure of all, which is arriving with a dead phone and no cord. The six picks here range from the GrnOas.E at 10000mAh and 22.5W to the OHOVIV at a huge 50000mAh. Between them sit two charmast models, plus the VRURC and Q, which add a fold-out AC wall plug.

The cable count is the real differentiator. The charmast lines carry four built-in cables for USB-C, iPhone, Micro-USB, and USB-A, while the Q and VRURC combine cables with a wall plug for charging the bank itself. The OHOVIV also offers four cables but in a much bigger body, which has consequences for travel.

We evaluated each pick on product specs and buyer feedback, weighing cable variety, charging speed, capacity, and size. The sections below rank the six, then show how to choose by cable type, budget, capacity, and trip type.

products.name: charmast 10000mAh 22.5W Power Bank With 4 Built-in Cables
products.description:
This charmast is the most complete built-in-cable charger in the group. It has three built-in output cables plus extra ports and can recharge in four ways, so it works with almost any wall adapter or laptop you own. At 22.5W the maker says it takes an iPhone 15 from empty to about 50 percent in half an hour.

Compatibility is wide, covering recent iPhones, Samsung Galaxy phones, and Google Pixel models. The tradeoff is the usual one for built-in cables, since a damaged cord cannot be swapped. Reinforced cables help, but a fixed cable is still a fixed cable.

It suits a family that shares one charger on trips. Compared with the other charmast listing, this one adds the 22.5W fast charging claim and an extra input. Compared with the GrnOas.E, it has more outputs and a bigger cable range, though the GrnOas.E is lower in cost.
products.bestFor: Families and travelers who want the broadest cable set with fast charging.
pros: Four ways to recharge the bank
Works with iPhone, Galaxy, and Pixel
cons: Busier body than a single-cable unit

products.name: charmast 10000mAh Power Bank With 4 Built-in Cables
products.description:
This charmast is the same family as the top pick, with four reinforced cables and six outputs, but it lists 3A fast charging instead of 22.5W. It can power up to six devices at once, which is rare at this capacity. For a household with older gadgets, the Micro-USB cable and USB-A cable are real conveniences.

The fast charging is slower than the 22.5W version, and sharing 10000mAh among six outputs means each device gets less. It is a better hub than a rocket. The cables are reinforced, but cannot be replaced if they fail.

The recharge options include USB-C, USB-A, and Micro-USB inputs, so you can use whatever cable is nearby. Compared with the 22.5W charmast, it costs less and omits the faster charging. Compared with the VRURC, it has more cables but no wall plug.
products.bestFor: Shared family charging on a tighter budget.
pros: Up to six devices at once

products.name: GrnOas.E 10000mAh 22.5W Power Bank
products.description:
The GrnOas.E is the lowest-cost pick here and still delivers PD and QC fast charging up to 22.5W. It measures 5.9 x 2.7 x 0.72 inches and weighs 8.4 oz, which is easy to carry in a bag. It offers four outputs and two inputs, with built-in cables.

A smart chip protects against overcharge, over-voltage, over-current, and short circuit. That is a useful safety feature for a low-cost unit. The tradeoff is that it has fewer cables and ports than either charmast model.

It makes sense as a simple second charger. Compared with the charmast lines, it has fewer outputs but the same capacity and similar speed. Compared with the VRURC, it lacks a wall plug but is cheaper.
products.bestFor: Budget shoppers who want fast charging and built-in cables without extras.
cons: Fewer cables and ports than the charmast models

products.name: VRURC 10000mAh Power Bank With AC Wall Plug
products.description:
The VRURC adds a built-in AC wall plug to its cables, so you can recharge the bank straight from an outlet without any adapter. It includes a Micro cable, a USB-C cable, and a cable for iPhone. At 5.9 x 2.8 x 0.7 inches and 8 oz it is comparable in size to the other 10000mAh models.

The maker claims it can power devices two and a half to four times depending on the device. The wall plug is the main appeal, because it removes a charger from your bag. The downside is that the plug adds thickness and the unit is not the fastest here.

It works well as a travel charger that doubles as a wall adapter. Compared with the Q, it offers a similar idea in a slightly different format. Compared with the GrnOas.E, it adds the plug but lacks the stated 22.5W speed.
products.bestFor: Travelers who want to skip a separate wall charger.
pros: Micro, USB-C, and iPhone cables included

products.name: Q 10000mAh Power Bank With AC Wall Plug and Cables
products.description:
The Q is a 5-in-1 travel charger that folds three cables and an AC wall plug into one body. It can power up to four devices at once, which suits a couple traveling together. Buyers do not need extra cables or adapters.

That all-in-one approach is convenient but offers little detail on output speed, so the Q is best for steady top-ups. As with other built-in designs, a damaged cable cannot be replaced. It is a good choice for people who value fewer items to pack.

Compared with the VRURC, it advertises more integration but gives fewer published dimensions. Compared with the charmast, it has fewer outputs but adds a wall plug. It is a middle option for people who want simplicity.
products.bestFor: Couples traveling who want one integrated charger.
pros: Wall plug and three cables built in

products.name: OHOVIV 50000mAh Power Bank With 4 Built-in Cables
products.description:
The OHOVIV is in a different league for capacity, at 50000mAh. The maker says it gives about ten charges for an iPhone 15 and can charge six devices at once through four built-in cables and three ports. For a camping trip, a long power cut, or a home backup, that endurance is unmatched here.

The cost is size and travel limits. At 3.7 volts, 50000mAh is about 185 Wh, which is above the 160 Wh airline ceiling, so it is not allowed in cabin bags. It is therefore a home, car, and camping charger rather than a flight companion.

It is heavy, so it will not slip into a pocket. Compared with the 10000mAh picks, it is roughly five times the energy for much more bulk. Compared with the charmast 22.5W, it matches the speed but is for stationary use.
products.bestFor: Home backup, camping, and road trips where weight and flying are not concerns.
cons: Too large for airline carry-on rules

buyingCriteria.explanation: Built-in cables only help if they match your devices. The charmast and OHOVIV cover USB-C, iPhone, Micro-USB, and USB-A, while the GrnOas.E offers fewer. If you own an older Micro-USB gadget, favor the charmast. For a USB-C-only household, any pick works.

Speed depends on watts, and USB-C Power Delivery spans 18 to 100W while USB-A ports often give only 5 to 12W. The charmast 22.5W, GrnOas.E, and OHOVIV all list up to 22.5W. The slower 3A charmast listing is fine for overnight or desk use. Choose 22.5W if your phone supports fast charging.

Compare watt-hours, not just milliamp hours, since Wh equals mAh divided by 1000 times the voltage, usually 3.6 to 3.7. A 10000mAh bank is about 37 Wh and the 50000mAh OHOVIV is about 185 Wh. Usable output is roughly 77 to 83 percent of the rating. Match capacity to the days you will be away from an outlet.

The common tiers are 100 Wh or less allowed in cabin, 100 to 160 Wh with airline approval, and nothing above 160 Wh. The 10000mAh picks are all around 37 Wh. The OHOVIV at about 185 Wh exceeds the ceiling and cannot fly. Check your airline before you pack.

Built-in cables are the weak point because they cannot be replaced. The charmast uses reinforced cables to reduce risk. Handle the cables gently and avoid sharp bends. If you are rough on gear, consider a unit with a detachable cable instead.

The VRURC and Q include an AC wall plug, which removes an adapter from your bag. The charmast offers three or four recharge inputs. A wall plug adds some thickness. Decide whether you would rather carry a separate adapter or accept a slightly chunkier body.

howWeEvaluated.title: Cable variety
howWeEvaluated.description: We compared the number and type of built-in cables, from the charmast's four to the GrnOas.E's simpler set. A cable that does not fit your device is useless. We rewarded variety and reinforced build. The strongest pick covered the most devices.

howWeEvaluated.title: Charging speed
howWeEvaluated.description: We compared stated output, including the 22.5W models and the slower 3A listing. Speed matters most for a nearly empty phone. We used manufacturer figures as claims, not measurements. The fastest picks were the charmast 22.5W, GrnOas.E, and OHOVIV.

howWeEvaluated.title: Capacity and travel
howWeEvaluated.description: We compared capacity from 10000mAh to the 50000mAh OHOVIV and checked it against airline limits. The OHOVIV is unmatched for endurance but cannot fly. The 10000mAh models are travel friendly.

howWeEvaluated.title: Extras and convenience
howWeEvaluated.description: We looked at wall plugs, input options, and device counts. The VRURC and Q include plugs, and the charmast offers many inputs. These extras reduce what you carry. The most basic design, the GrnOas.E, has fewer.

howWeEvaluated.title: Value and support
howWeEvaluated.description: We weighed relative price tier against features, with the GrnOas.E the lowest-cost pick and the OHOVIV the premium one. We considered safety protections such as the GrnOas.E's smart chip.

cards.label: Carry-on friendly
cards.text: The charmast models, GrnOas.E, VRURC, and Q are all about 37 Wh. They fit airline rules. Recommended for flights.

cards.label: Home or camping
cards.text: The OHOVIV at 50000mAh is about 185 Wh and cannot fly. It suits outages and road trips. Recommended for stationary use.

howToChoose.note: Pick a 10000mAh unit for flights and the OHOVIV for home.

cards.label: Look for
cards.text: Several outputs and cable types so every device can charge, plus carry-on compliance.

cards.label: In this comparison
cards.text: The charmast 22.5W offers six outputs and four recharge inputs, which suits a family. The Q suits a couple who want a wall plug.

cards.label: Spend more if
cards.text: You need days of power at home or camp, where the OHOVIV makes sense. You also want fast charging with many cables, as the charmast 22.5W provides.

cards.label: Save if
cards.text: You only need a simple top-up, where the GrnOas.E is enough. The lower-cost charmast adds more cables.

faq.q: How do I choose between these chargers with built-in cables?
faq.a: Start with the cable types you need and whether you will fly. The charmast models cover the most devices, the VRURC and Q add wall plugs, and the OHOVIV maximizes capacity. Match the pick to your trips.

faq.q: How much should I spend on a charger with built-in cables?
faq.a: The GrnOas.E is the lowest-cost pick and still offers 22.5W. The charmast models are mid-range with more cables. The OHOVIV costs more for its huge capacity.
They are convenient but cannot be replaced if damaged. The charmast uses reinforced cables to reduce that risk. Avoid sharp bends and tugging.

faq.q: Can I take the OHOVIV 50000mAh on a plane?
faq.a: No, a 50000mAh bank is about 185 Wh, which is above the 160 Wh limit. Power banks must also go in carry-on bags. Use it at home or in the car.

faq.q: Is a wall plug worth having?
faq.a: It removes a separate adapter from your bag, which helps travelers. The tradeoff is some extra thickness. The VRURC and Q include one.

faq.q: Why does my phone charge slowly from the built-in cable?
faq.a: The output may be limited, as with a 3A listing, or the phone may not support the protocol. Use a 22.5W model like the charmast 22.5W. USB-A outputs often give only 5 to 12W.

faq.q: How many times will 10000mAh charge my phone?
faq.a: Usable energy is roughly 77 to 83 percent of the rating, so expect about one to two refills. Larger phones use more. Charging several devices at once reduces that.
